title: PSU dividend jackpot! ONGC vs NTPC vs CONCOR vs Petronet: Who offers highest payout? Record date, technical targets | Stock Market News
text:
PSU dividend comparison: Oil and Natural Gas Corporation, NTPC, Container Corporation of India, and Petronet LNG are some of the key companies which have announced dividends for the financial year 2026-27.

Record dates for dividend announced by most of these PSUs is set to fall in the coming days. For investors who closely track developments around PSU dividends, here are all the details from their payout amount, dividend record dates to technical targets by experts.

Petronet LNG is a government promoted joint venture and is not classified as PSU. However, it has been included in the comparison as it's backed by four PSUs, ie BPCL, ONGC, GAIL and IOC.

Out of the four companies, ONGC has announced the highest payout for the financial year 2026-27. The PSU has fixed November 12 as the record date.

ONGC’s board of directors announced an interim dividend of ₹8 per equity share with a face value of ₹5 each. The company has fixed November 12, 2026 as the record date to determine eligibility of investors for the payout.

The stock closed 1.90% lower at ₹230.10 per share on BSE with a market capitalisation of ₹2,89,472.22 crore on Thursday. The PSU stock reclaimed its 20 day exponential moving average “(EMA) with RSI above 50, providing a buy-on-dips entry at ₹226.00 ₹229.00 (SL: ₹221.00, Targets: ₹238.00 / ₹245.00),” stated Virat Jagad Sr. Technical Research Analyst at Bonanza.

NTPC’s board of directors announced the first interim dividend at the rate of 30% on the face value of ₹10 each. Which means that the PSU has announced ₹3 per share dividend. NTPC dividend record date is fixed as November 6, 2026.

Shares of NTPC closed 1.65% lower at ₹316.40 per share on BSE with a market capitalisation of ₹3,06,802.52 crore on Thursday. The PSU stock has bounced off ₹295 support to reclaim its 20 EMA at ₹314.27 per share.

According to Virat Jagad, the movement has set up a fresh entry point at ₹314- ₹317. The expert recommends to maintain stop loss at ₹304 per share and target at ₹325- ₹333 per share.

CONCOR’s board of directors approved ₹1.90 per equity share dividend and has fixed November 11 as the record date.

Shares of CONCOR closed 3.29% higher at ₹440 per share on BSE on Thursday. The PSU stock is staging a mean-reversion recovery off ₹410 lows, and the momentum is supporting a dip entry at ₹432- ₹440 per share. Investors can maintain a stop loss at ₹415 per share and target at ₹453- ₹470 per share, according to Jagad.

Petronet LNG’s board of directors considered and approved ₹7 per equity share dividend. The company has fixed November 6 as the record date.

The company scrip closed 2.16% higher at ₹316.80 per share on BSE on Thursday. According to Virat Jagad, the energy stock is trading strongly above all key EMAs with an RSI of 69. Investors can consider fresh entry at ₹305- ₹312, and maintain a stop loss of ₹294 and target for ₹330- ₹345.
